     1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]
   133	  Integrating against $\mu$ and applying Tonelli's theorem proves
   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}
   138	
   139	\subsection{Temporal completion and the original noise}
   140	
   141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a
   145	    = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s
   146	  \]
   147	  is positive semidefinite on real compact smooth tests. Its null-quotient
   148	  completion $H_a$ is separable. The inclusion of tests extends continuously
   149	  from $L^2(0,T)$, with
   150	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-time-schur}
   151	    \|f\|_a^2 \le \frac{2T^{1-a}}{1-a}\|f\|_2^2.
   152	  \end{equation}
   153	  In its complexification the norm is given by the same double integral with
   154	  $f(t)\overline{f(s)}$. In particular, bounded measurable amplitudes on a
   155	  subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion.
   156	\end{lemma}
   157	
   158	\begin{proof}
   159	  Write $\Gamma_E$ for Euler's Gamma function. Away from the null diagonal,
   160	  \[
   161	    |t-s|^{-a} = \frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty
   162	    \lambda^{a-1}e^{-\lambda|t-s|}\ud\lambda.
   163	  \]
   164	  This follows by substitution in the defining Gamma integral. Moreover,
   165	  \[
   166	    e^{-\lambda|t-s|}
   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.
   169	  \]
   170	  For each $\lambda > 0$ its quadratic form is an integral of a square. All
   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the
   172	  kernel row integral is at most $2T^{1-a}/(1-a)$. The same bound and $2|xy| \le
   173	  |x|^2+|y|^2$ prove~\eqref{E:masked-time-schur}. A countable $L^2$-dense family
   174	  of compact smooth tests is consequently dense in $H_a$, proving separability.
   175	  The complex quadratic form is the sum of those of the real and imaginary
   176	  parts, since symmetry cancels the imaginary cross term. Thus, the same bound
   177	  holds after complexification. Smooth density in $L^2$, together with the Schur
   178	  bound on the absolute bilinear form, extends the inclusion and the integral
   179	  identity to $L^2$. This includes the stated interval amplitudes. This proves
   180	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   181	\end{proof}
   182	
   183	Let $\mathcal{D}$ consist of finite sums $F(t,x) = \sum_j\tau_j(t)f_j(x)$ with
   184	real $\tau_j \in C_c^\infty(0,T)$ and real Schwartz $f_j$. These give
   185	$H_a$-valued Schwartz functions of $x$. Let $W$ denote the original real
   186	isonormal noise in~\eqref{E:cov}.
   187	
   188	\begin{proposition}[Completion on the same noise]\label{P:masked-noise-completion}
   189	  The space $\mathcal{D}$ belongs to the original test-noise completion and
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}
   191	    \E W(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   192	    \|\widehat{F}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  Define the auxiliary seminorm
   195	  \[
   196	    N_R(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   197	    \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
   198	  \]
   199	  Then $F \mapsto W(\zeta_RF)$ extends as a contraction from the null-quotient
   200	  completion for $N_R$ into the original $L^2(\Omega)$. The extension is
   201	  centered and jointly Gaussian. For finitely many real $F_1,\ldots,F_m \in
   202	  \mathcal{D}$, their masked covariance matrix is bounded in positive
   203	  semidefinite order by the matrix of auxiliary inner products. This gives
   204	  covariance comparison for every finite linear Gaussian image and every convex
   205	  norm power $p \ge 1$.
   206	\end{proposition}
   207	
   208	\begin{proof}
   209	  For real spatial Schwartz $f,g$, put $h(z) = \int f(y+z)g(y)\ud y$. Fourier
   210	  inversion and Parseval give
   211	  \[
   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]
   215	  Therefore,
   216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]
   220	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single test $h$ and reflect
   221	  $\xi$ using evenness of $\mu$. The spatial covariance is thus
   222	  $(2\pi)^d\int\widehat{f}(\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Summing
   223	  over the finitely many temporal factors gives
   224	  \eqref{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}. Schwartz decay, temperedness and temporal
   225	  integrability justify these pairings. If $W$ is initially given only on
   226	  compact spatial tests, smooth expanding cutoffs converge in the Schwartz
   227	  topology. The spectral form is continuous in that topology, admitting
   228	  $\mathcal{D}$ in the same completion.
   229	
   230	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, applied with $H =
   231	  H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$, gives $\E W(\zeta_RF)^2 \le N_R(F)^2$. It annihilates
   232	  auxiliary-null tests. An auxiliary Cauchy sequence thus gives a Cauchy
   233	  sequence of noise evaluations in $L^2(\Omega)$, proving the contraction
   234	  extension and its uniqueness. Every finite linear combination of the limits is
   235	  an $L^2$ limit of centered Gaussian variables. Their variances converge, so
   236	  their characteristic functions prove that the limits remain jointly centered
   237	  Gaussian.
   238	
   239	  For the finite family let $A$ be the covariance matrix and $B$ the auxiliary
   240	  Gram matrix. Applying the norm inequality to $\sum_i b_iF_i$ gives
   241	  $b^{\mathsf{T}}Ab \le b^{\mathsf{T}}Bb$ for every real vector $b$.
   242	  Diagonalizing $B-A$ constructs a centered Gaussian vector $Z$ of that
   243	  covariance, independent of the evaluation vector $X$, on a product space. Then
   244	  $X+Z$ has covariance $B$. Conditional Jensen gives $\E\|X\|^p \le \E\|X+Z\|^p$
   245	  for every norm and $p \ge 1$. Finite Gaussian moments ensure finiteness of
   246	  both sides. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion}.
   247	\end{proof}
   248	
   249	The auxiliary completion depends on $R$ and $\zeta$. Its construction does not
   250	define multiplication by $\zeta_R$ on the original noise quotient. Nor does the
   251	finite linear Gaussian comparison assert a covariance comparison for nonlinear
   252	wave solutions. The auxiliary and original test norms need not dominate one
   253	another. No spatial representative for every auxiliary class, nonnegative
   254	physical inverse covariance for $\nu_R$, or uniform density bound in $R$ is
   255	asserted.
   256	
   257	\begin{proposition}[A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests]
   258	  \label{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}
   259	  In the admissible case $d = 2$, $\alpha = 1$, $0 < a < 1$ and $\Gamma =
   260	  \delta_0(\ud x_1)\ud x_2$, there is a real compact smooth mask $\zeta$ such
   261	  that no finite $C$ satisfies $\E W(\zeta F)^2 \le C\E W(F)^2$ for every
   262	  compact smooth test $F$.
   263	\end{proposition}
   264	
   265	\begin{proof}
   266	  Fourier inversion on Schwartz tests gives $\mu =
   267	  (2\pi)^{-1}\ud\xi_1\delta_0(\ud\xi_2)$ in the stated spectral convention. The
   268	  measure $\Gamma$ is nonnegative, even, positive definite and tempered, with
   269	  $\Gamma(cA) = c\Gamma(A)$. It therefore satisfies Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}
   270	  with $\alpha = 1$. This is not spatial white noise in dimension two. For real
   271	  compact smooth $g$, its spatial covariance is, by ordinary Fubini,
   272	  \[
   273	    V(g) = \int_\R\left(\int_\R g(x_1,x_2)\ud x_2\right)^2\ud x_1.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose real even $\chi \in C_c^\infty(\R)$ equal to one on $[-1,1]$ and zero
   276	  outside $[-2,2]$. For example, on $1 < r = |x| < 2$ use
   277	  \[
   278	    \chi(x) = \frac{e^{-1/(2-r)}}{e^{-1/(2-r)}+e^{-1/(r-1)}}.
   279	  \]
   280	  The endpoint exponentials vanish to every order, so the plateau pastes
   281	  smoothly. Let $I_\chi = \int(\chi')^2 > 0$ and $J_\chi = \int\chi^4 > 0$.
   282	  Positivity of $I_\chi$ follows because $\chi$ is not constant, and $J_\chi \ge
   283	  2$. Put $g(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi''(x_2)$ and $\zeta(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi(x_2)$.
   284	  Their unmasked marginal vanishes since $\int\chi'' = 0$, whereas integration
   285	  by parts gives the masked marginal $-I_\chi\chi(x_1)^2$. Thus, $V(g) = 0$ and
   286	  $V(\zeta g) = J_\chi I_\chi^2 > 0$. For a nonzero nonnegative $\tau \in
   287	  C_c^\infty(0,T)$, set $F(t,x) = \tau(t)g(x)$. The temporal factor
   288	  $\|\tau\|_a^2$ is finite and strictly positive because its nonnegative
   289	  integrand is positive on a set of positive two-dimensional measure.
   290	  Consequently, the full unmasked variance is zero and the masked variance is
   291	  positive. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}.
   292	\end{proof}

   294	\subsection{Temporal modulation and continuous wave factors}
   295	
   296	Write $\langle x\rangle = \sqrt{1+x^2}$. Let $I = [s,s+h] \subset [0,T]$, with
   297	$0 < h \le 1$. Norms below are those of the complexified temporal completion in
   298	Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   299	
   300	\begin{lemma}[Modulated amplitudes]\label{L:masked-temporal-modulation}
   301	  Let $A \in C^1(I;\mathbb{C})$, $M = \sup_I|A|$ and $D = \sup_I|A'|$. For every
   302	  real $\omega$,
   303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-temporal-modulation}
   304	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   305	    \le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\langle h\omega\rangle^{a-1},
   306	    \qquad C_0(a) = \frac{16}{1-a}.
   307	  \end{equation}
   308	  The bound is uniform in $T,s,h,A$ and $\omega$.
   309	\end{lemma}
   310	
   311	\begin{proof}
   312	  Put $c(v) = \int_s^{s+h-v}A(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u$ for $0 \le v \le h$.
   313	  Differentiation at the moving endpoint gives
   314	  \[
   315	    c'(v) = -A(s+h)\overline{A(s+h-v)}
   316	    +\int_s^{s+h-v}A'(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u.
   317	  \]
   318	  Thus, $c(h) = 0$, $|c(v)| \le hM^2$ and $|c'(v)| \le M^2+hMD$. Splitting the
   319	  covariance square into its two conjugate triangles gives
   320	  \[
   321	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}
   346	
   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}
   377	
   378	\begin{lemma}[Continuous sine factors]\label{L:masked-continuous-wave}
   379	  Define $c_r(t) = \cos(rt)$ and
   380	  \[
   381	    b_r(t) = \langle r\rangle\frac{\sin(rt)}r\quad(r > 0),
   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]
   384	  For $F_r \in \{c_r,b_r\}$ and $G_\rho \in \{c_\rho,b_\rho\}$,
   385	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-continuous-wave}
   386	    \|1_IF_rG_\rho\|_a^2
   387	    \le C_1(a)(1+T)^4h^{2-a}\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   388	    \qquad C_1(a) = 4\cdot3^{1-a}C_0(a).
   389	  \end{equation}
   390	\end{lemma}
   391	
   392	\begin{proof}
   393	  For $r \ge 1$, $b_r$ is a sine times a coefficient at most $\sqrt{2}$. For $0
   394	  \le r \le 1$, the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
   395	  \[
   396	    b_r(t) = t\langle r\rangle\int_0^1\cos(vrt)\ud v.
   397	  \]
   398	  This includes $r = 0$. Hence, a product $F_rG_\rho$ is a scalar coefficient of
   399	  absolute value at most two times a normalized integral of
   400	  $t^jP_{r'}(t)Q_{\rho'}(t)$, where $j \in \{0,1,2\}$ and $|r'-r|,|\rho'-\rho|
   401	  \le 1$. The integral is over zero, one or two copies of $[0,1]$; with no
   402	  averages, use a one-point probability space. Its parameter dependence is
   403	  continuous in $L^2(0,T)$ by dominated convergence.
   404	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} makes it continuous in $H_a$ as well.
   405	  Thus, the averages are Bochner integrals, and their $H_a$ images agree with
   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
   408	
   409	  Apply Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products} to each integrand with $A(t) = t^j$.
   410	  For $j = 0,1,2$, respectively, $M+hD$ is at most $1$, $T+1$ and $T^2+2T$. In
   411	  every case $(M+hD)^2 \le (1+T)^4$. For real $x,e$, the triangle inequality and
   412	  its reverse imply
   413	  \[
   414	    \frac{\langle x\rangle}{1+|e|}
   415	    \le \langle x+e\rangle \le (1+|e|)\langle x\rangle.
   416	  \]
   417	  The changes in $h(r\pm\rho)$ have magnitude at most two, since $h \le 1$.
   418	  Because $a-1 < 0$, each altered bracket to the power $a-1$ is at most
   419	  $3^{1-a}$ times the original one. Apply these comparisons, Hilbert Jensen and
   420	  the squared scalar coefficient bound four to obtain
   421	  \eqref{E:masked-continuous-wave}. This proves
   422	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}.
   423	\end{proof}
   424	
   425	These estimates concern covariance forms and temporal factors. Their application
   426	to displacement and velocity is in Section~\ref{S:wave-variance}; the subsequent
   427	operator, source and moment results require their separate proofs. They do not
   428	follow from covariance domination alone.

  1758	Formalizes `L:masked-continuous-wave` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
  1759	at `975feb3`, statement lines 378-390, display `E:masked-continuous-wave`
  1760	lines 385-389, proof lines 392-423) with the standing assumptions of its
  1761	subsection (lines 296-298) and the hypotheses `T > 0`, `0 < a < 1` of
  1762	`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 141-156). The factors are
  1763	`c_r(t) = cos(rt)` (`cFn`) and `b_r(t) = <r> sin(rt)/r` for `r > 0`,
  1764	`b_0(t) = t` (`bFn`; lines 379-383). `Wave` and `Wave.eval` give the choices
  1765	`F_r` in `{c_r, b_r}`, `G_rho` in `{c_rho, b_rho}` (line 384). `waveFn I F G r rho`
  1766	is `1_I F_r G_rho` with real values viewed in `C`. `C_1` is
  1767	`4 * 3^(1-a) * C_0(a)` (line 388), with `C_0(a) = 16/(1-a)` from
  1768	`MaskedTrigProducts`.
  1769	
  1770	What is stated. The manuscript's left side is the norm of the complexified
  1771	temporal completion `H_a^C` (lines 297-298). As in
  1772	`MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`, this norm is modelled
  1773	abstractly. `E` is a complex inner product space. `V` is a submodule of
  1774	`R -> C`, the functions accepted into the completion. `emb : V -> E` is a
  1775	linear inclusion, and `||f||_a` is `||emb f||`. `H_a` is not built in this
  1776	module. The wrapper `masked_continuous_wave_paper` takes the manuscript's
  1777	hypotheses: `0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `0 < h <= 1`, `0 <= s`, `s + h <= T`,
  1778	`r, rho >= 0`, `F, G` in `{c, b}`. It also takes the same two supplied
  1779	inputs as `masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`, under the same names.
  1780	`hmem` says that for every `A` that is `C^1` on `I = [s, s+h]`
  1781	(`ContDiffOn R 1 A I`) and every real `omega`, `1_I A e^(i omega t)` lies in
  1782	`V`. This is B24's `hmem` quantified over every amplitude B24 accepts. Its
  1783	source is `L:masked-time-completion`, lines 154-155: bounded measurable
  1784	amplitudes on a subinterval, extended by zero, belong to the completion. A
  1785	function that is `C^1` on the compact `I` is bounded there and measurable
  1786	after extension by zero, so the input asks for no more than its source.
  1787	`hnorm` is B24's `hnorm` verbatim: for `f` in `V` with `f` in `L^2(0,T)`,
  1788	`||emb f||^2 = Re timeForm a T f f`. This is the complexification clause of
  1789	`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 153-154, with lines 148-149 and 177-179).
  1790	The conclusion has two parts. First, `1_I F_r G_rho` lies in `V`. Second,
  1791	for that element, `||emb(1_I F_r G_rho)||^2 <= C_1(a) (1+T)^4 h^(2-a) Q_h(r,rho)`,
  1792	which is `E:masked-continuous-wave` with the manuscript's constant. No
  1793	`Gamma != 0` is assumed, and the TeX states none.
  1794	
  1795	Implicit side conditions made explicit. The functions are real-valued and
  1796	enter `V` through the coercion `R -> C`. `bFn r` is also defined for
  1797	`r < 0`, but that value is never used, because `r, rho >= 0` are hypotheses.

  1799	the nonempty set `I` (since `h > 0`) of bounded sets, so they are not Lean's
  1800	junk value. `C_0(a)` is the junk-free `16/(1-a)` because `a < 1`, and the
  1801	brackets raised to real powers are at least `1`.

  1808	(lines 393-398). It then forms `H_a`-valued Bochner averages over up to two

  1810	`L:masked-trig-products` with `A(t) = t^j` (lines 409-411) and compares
  1811	brackets (lines 411-419). Lean uses no averaging and no continuity of a
  1812	parameter family in `H_a`. Each factor is split into an amplitude, a

    13	`0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `I = [s, s+h] ⊆ [0, T]` (`0 ≤ s`, `s + h ≤ T`),

    17	`1_I F_r G_ρ` (`waveFn`) lies in the accepted class `V`, and

    27	accepted into the completion) and a linear inclusion `emb : V →ₗ[ℂ] E`; the

    31	  `A ∈ C¹(I; ℂ)` and every real `ω`, `1_I A e^{iω·} ∈ V`.  Source:
    32	  `L:masked-time-completion`, TeX lines 154-155 ("bounded measurable
    33	  amplitudes on a subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion"),
    34	  which covers every such `A` (continuous on the compact `I`, hence bounded and
    35	  measurable after extension by zero); so the input is no stronger than its

    37	* `hnorm` — verbatim B24's `hnorm`: for `f ∈ V` with `f ∈ L²(0,T)`,
    38	  `‖emb f‖² = Re ∬_{[0,T]²} f(t) conj f(u) |t-u|^{-a}`.  Source: the

    45	Proof route (differs from the TeX proof; same statement, same constant).  The
    46	TeX (lines 392-423) writes `b_r = t⟨r⟩∫_0^1 cos(vrt) dv` for `r ≤ 1`, takes
    47	`H_a`-valued Bochner averages over `[0,1]^k`, applies Hilbert Jensen and
    48	`L:masked-trig-products` with `A(t) = t^j` to each integrand at frequencies
    49	`r', ρ'` with `|r'-r|, |ρ'-ρ| ≤ 1`, and compares brackets.  Here no averaging
    50	and no continuity of a parameter family in `H_a` is used.  Instead:
    51	* each factor is written as an amplitude times a trigonometric factor
    52	  (`amp`, `trig`, `fr`; `eval_eq`): `c_r = 1·cos(r·)`; for `r ≥ 1`,
    53	  `b_r = (⟨r⟩/r)·sin(r·)`, the coefficient `⟨r⟩/r ≤ √2` going into the
    54	  amplitude; for `r < 1` (including `r = 0`), `b_r = b_r·cos(0·)`, the whole
    55	  factor going into the amplitude at frequency `0`;

    99	
   100	/-- `c_r(t) = cos(rt)` (TeX line 379). -/
   101	def cFn (r t : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.cos (r * t)

   103	/-- `b_r(t) = ⟨r⟩ sin(rt)/r` for `r ≠ 0` and `b_0(t) = t` (TeX lines 380-383;
   104	the manuscript defines it for `r > 0` and `r = 0`, and only `r ≥ 0` is used). -/
   105	def bFn (r t : ℝ) : ℝ := if r = 0 then t else bracket r * Real.sin (r * t) / r

   109	  | c
   110	  | b

   112	/-- `Wave.eval W r t` is `c_r(t)` or `b_r(t)`. -/

   114	  | .c, r, t => cFn r t
   115	  | .b, r, t => bFn r t

   117	/-- The masked product `t ↦ 1_I(t) F_r(t) G_ρ(t)`, viewed in `ℂ`. -/
   118	def waveFn (I : Set ℝ) (F G : Wave) (r ρ : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ :=
   119	  I.indicator fun t => ((F.eval r t * G.eval ρ t : ℝ) : ℂ)

   125	
   126	/-- `⟨x+e⟩ ≤ (1+|e|)⟨x⟩` (upper half of the display at TeX lines 413-416, on line 415). -/
   127	theorem bracket_add_le (x e : ℝ) : bracket (x + e) ≤ (1 + |e|) * bracket x := by
   128	  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 + |e| := by positivity
   129	  have hx : 2 * |x| ≤ 1 + x ^ 2 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (|x| - 1), sq_abs x]
   130	  have hxe : x * e ≤ |x| * |e| := (le_abs_self _).trans_eq (abs_mul x e)
   131	  have key : 1 + (x + e) ^ 2 ≤ ((1 + |e|) * bracket x) ^ 2 := by
   132	    rw [mul_pow, bracket, Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity)]
   133	    nlinarith [abs_nonneg e, sq_abs e, mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg e) (sq_nonneg (|x| - 1)),
   134	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hx (abs_nonneg e), mul_nonneg (abs_nonneg e) (sq_nonneg x),
   135	      sq_nonneg (e * x)]
   136	  rw [bracket, Real.sqrt_le_iff]
   137	  exact ⟨mul_nonneg h1 (Real.sqrt_nonneg _), key⟩
   138	
   139	/-- `⟨x⟩ > 0`. -/
   140	theorem bracket_pos (x : ℝ) : 0 < bracket x := lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos (one_le_bracket x)
   141	
   142	/-- If `|x - x'| ≤ 2` and `a < 1`, then `⟨x'⟩^{a-1} ≤ 3^{1-a} ⟨x⟩^{a-1}` (TeX
   143	lines 418-419: "each altered bracket to the power `a-1` is at most `3^{1-a}`
   144	times the original one"). -/
   145	theorem bracket_rpow_shift_le {a : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) {x x' : ℝ} (hxx : |x - x'| ≤ 2) :
   146	    bracket x' ^ (a - 1) ≤ 3 ^ (1 - a) * bracket x ^ (a - 1) := by
   147	  have hb : bracket x ≤ 3 * bracket x' := by
   148	    have := bracket_add_le x' (x - x')
   149	    rw [add_sub_cancel] at this
   150	    refine this.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (bracket_pos x').le)
   151	    linarith
   152	  have hr : (3 * bracket x') ^ (a - 1) ≤ bracket x ^ (a - 1) :=
   153	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos (bracket_pos x) hb (by linarith)
   154	  rw [Real.mul_rpow (by norm_num) (bracket_pos x').le] at hr
   155	  have h3 : (3 : ℝ) ^ (1 - a) * 3 ^ (a - 1) = 1 := by
   156	    rw [← Real.rpow_add (by norm_num)]; simp
   157	  have h3p : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 3 ^ (1 - a) := by positivity
   158	  calc bracket x' ^ (a - 1) = 3 ^ (1 - a) * (3 ^ (a - 1) * bracket x' ^ (a - 1)) := by
   159	        rw [← mul_assoc, h3, one_mul]
   160	    _ ≤ 3 ^ (1 - a) * bracket x ^ (a - 1) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hr h3p

   162	/-- Frequency shifts by at most one in each variable cost at most `3^{1-a}`:
   163	for `0 ≤ h ≤ 1`, `|r'-r| ≤ 1`, `|ρ'-ρ| ≤ 1`, `𝒬_h(r',ρ') ≤ 3^{1-a} 𝒬_h(r,ρ)`
   164	(TeX lines 417-419, "the changes in `h(r±ρ)` have magnitude at most two"). -/
   165	theorem frequencyPair_shift_le {a h r ρ r' ρ' : ℝ} (ha1 : a < 1) (hh0 : 0 ≤ h) (hh1 : h ≤ 1)
   166	    (hr : |r - r'| ≤ 1) (hρ : |ρ - ρ'| ≤ 1) :
   167	    frequencyPair a h r' ρ' ≤ 3 ^ (1 - a) * frequencyPair a h r ρ := by
   168	  obtain ⟨hr1, hr2⟩ := abs_le.mp hr
   169	  obtain ⟨hρ1, hρ2⟩ := abs_le.mp hρ
   170	  have d1 : |h * (r - ρ) - h * (r' - ρ')| ≤ 2 := by
   171	    rw [abs_le]; constructor <;> nlinarith
   172	  have d2 : |h * (r + ρ) - h * (r' + ρ')| ≤ 2 := by
   173	    rw [abs_le]; constructor <;> nlinarith
   174	  unfold frequencyPair
   175	  rw [mul_add (3 ^ (1 - a) : ℝ)]
   176	  exact add_le_add (bracket_rpow_shift_le ha1 d1) (bracket_rpow_shift_le ha1 d2)

     1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]
   133	  Integrating against $\mu$ and applying Tonelli's theorem proves
   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}

   139	\subsection{Temporal completion and the original noise}
   140

141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a
   145	    = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s
   146	  \]
   147	  is positive semidefinite on real compact smooth tests. Its null-quotient
   148	  completion $H_a$ is separable. The inclusion of tests extends continuously
   149	  from $L^2(0,T)$, with
   150	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-time-schur}
   151	    \|f\|_a^2 \le \frac{2T^{1-a}}{1-a}\|f\|_2^2.
   152	  \end{equation}
   153	  In its complexification the norm is given by the same double integral with
   154	  $f(t)\overline{f(s)}$. In particular, bounded measurable amplitudes on a
   155	  subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion.
   156	\end{lemma}
   157	
   158	\begin{proof}
   159	  Write $\Gamma_E$ for Euler's Gamma function. Away from the null diagonal,
   160	  \[
   161	    |t-s|^{-a} = \frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty
   162	    \lambda^{a-1}e^{-\lambda|t-s|}\ud\lambda.
   163	  \]
   164	  This follows by substitution in the defining Gamma integral. Moreover,
   165	  \[
   166	    e^{-\lambda|t-s|}
   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.
   169	  \]
   170	  For each $\lambda > 0$ its quadratic form is an integral of a square. All
   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the
   172	  kernel row integral is at most $2T^{1-a}/(1-a)$. The same bound and $2|xy| \le
   173	  |x|^2+|y|^2$ prove~\eqref{E:masked-time-schur}. A countable $L^2$-dense family
   174	  of compact smooth tests is consequently dense in $H_a$, proving separability.
   175	  The complex quadratic form is the sum of those of the real and imaginary
   176	  parts, since symmetry cancels the imaginary cross term. Thus, the same bound
   177	  holds after complexification. Smooth density in $L^2$, together with the Schur
   178	  bound on the absolute bilinear form, extends the inclusion and the integral
   179	  identity to $L^2$. This includes the stated interval amplitudes. This proves
   180	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   181	\end{proof}
   182	
   183	Let $\mathcal{D}$ consist of finite sums $F(t,x) = \sum_j\tau_j(t)f_j(x)$ with
   184	real $\tau_j \in C_c^\infty(0,T)$ and real Schwartz $f_j$. These give
   185	$H_a$-valued Schwartz functions of $x$. Let $W$ denote the original real
   186	isonormal noise in~\eqref{E:cov}.

   188	\begin{proposition}[Completion on the same noise]\label{P:masked-noise-completion}
   189	  The space $\mathcal{D}$ belongs to the original test-noise completion and
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}
   191	    \E W(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   192	    \|\widehat{F}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  Define the auxiliary seminorm
   195	  \[
   196	    N_R(F)^2 = (2\pi)^d\int
   197	    \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
   198	  \]
   199	  Then $F \mapsto W(\zeta_RF)$ extends as a contraction from the null-quotient
   200	  completion for $N_R$ into the original $L^2(\Omega)$. The extension is
   201	  centered and jointly Gaussian. For finitely many real $F_1,\ldots,F_m \in
   202	  \mathcal{D}$, their masked covariance matrix is bounded in positive
   203	  semidefinite order by the matrix of auxiliary inner products. This gives
   204	  covariance comparison for every finite linear Gaussian image and every convex
   205	  norm power $p \ge 1$.
   206	\end{proposition}
   207	
   208	\begin{proof}
   209	  For real spatial Schwartz $f,g$, put $h(z) = \int f(y+z)g(y)\ud y$. Fourier
   210	  inversion and Parseval give
   211	  \[
   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]
   215	  Therefore,
   216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]
   220	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single test $h$ and reflect
   221	  $\xi$ using evenness of $\mu$. The spatial covariance is thus
   222	  $(2\pi)^d\int\widehat{f}(\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\mu(\ud\xi)$. Summing
   223	  over the finitely many temporal factors gives
   224	  \eqref{E:masked-actual-noise-norm}. Schwartz decay, temperedness and temporal
   225	  integrability justify these pairings. If $W$ is initially given only on
   226	  compact spatial tests, smooth expanding cutoffs converge in the Schwartz
   227	  topology. The spectral form is continuous in that topology, admitting
   228	  $\mathcal{D}$ in the same completion.
   229	
   230	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}, applied with $H =
   231	  H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$, gives $\E W(\zeta_RF)^2 \le N_R(F)^2$. It annihilates
   232	  auxiliary-null tests. An auxiliary Cauchy sequence thus gives a Cauchy
   233	  sequence of noise evaluations in $L^2(\Omega)$, proving the contraction
   234	  extension and its uniqueness. Every finite linear combination of the limits is
   235	  an $L^2$ limit of centered Gaussian variables. Their variances converge, so
   236	  their characteristic functions prove that the limits remain jointly centered
   237	  Gaussian.
   238	
   239	  For the finite family let $A$ be the covariance matrix and $B$ the auxiliary
   240	  Gram matrix. Applying the norm inequality to $\sum_i b_iF_i$ gives
   241	  $b^{\mathsf{T}}Ab \le b^{\mathsf{T}}Bb$ for every real vector $b$.
   242	  Diagonalizing $B-A$ constructs a centered Gaussian vector $Z$ of that
   243	  covariance, independent of the evaluation vector $X$, on a product space. Then
   244	  $X+Z$ has covariance $B$. Conditional Jensen gives $\E\|X\|^p \le \E\|X+Z\|^p$
   245	  for every norm and $p \ge 1$. Finite Gaussian moments ensure finiteness of
   246	  both sides. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion}.
   247	\end{proof}

   249	The auxiliary completion depends on $R$ and $\zeta$. Its construction does not

    64	seminormed space (in particular in any complex inner product space). -/
    65	theorem norm_sq_sum_le {ι E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
    66	    (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → E) :
    67	    ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ^ 2 ≤
    68	      (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 := by
    69	  have htri : ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ := by
    70	    refine (norm_sum_le _ _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    71	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => norm_smul _ _
    72	  have hcs : (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 ≤
    73	      (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 := by
    74	    have key := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq s (fun j => Real.sqrt ‖c j‖)
    75	      (fun j => Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖)
    76	    have e1 : ∀ j, Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * (Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) = ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ :=
    77	      fun j => by rw [← mul_assoc, Real.mul_self_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)]
    78	    have e2 : ∀ j, Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ ^ 2 = ‖c j‖ :=
    79	      fun j => Real.sq_sqrt (norm_nonneg _)
    80	    have e3 : ∀ j, (Real.sqrt ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 = ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖ ^ 2 :=
    81	      fun j => by rw [mul_pow, e2]
    82	    simp only [e1, e2, e3] at key
    83	    exact key
    84	  have h0 : 0 ≤ ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ := norm_nonneg _
    85	  calc ‖∑ j ∈ s, c j • v j‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * ‖v j‖) ^ 2 :=
    86	        pow_le_pow_left₀ h0 htri 2
    87	    _ ≤ _ := hcs

   294	\subsection{Temporal modulation and continuous wave factors}
   295	
   296	Write $\langle x\rangle = \sqrt{1+x^2}$. Let $I = [s,s+h] \subset [0,T]$, with
   297	$0 < h \le 1$. Norms below are those of the complexified temporal completion in
   298	Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   299	
   300	\begin{lemma}[Modulated amplitudes]\label{L:masked-temporal-modulation}
   301	  Let $A \in C^1(I;\mathbb{C})$, $M = \sup_I|A|$ and $D = \sup_I|A'|$. For every
   302	  real $\omega$,
   303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-temporal-modulation}
   304	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   305	    \le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\langle h\omega\rangle^{a-1},
   306	    \qquad C_0(a) = \frac{16}{1-a}.
   307	  \end{equation}
   308	  The bound is uniform in $T,s,h,A$ and $\omega$.
   309	\end{lemma}
   310	
   311	\begin{proof}
   312	  Put $c(v) = \int_s^{s+h-v}A(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u$ for $0 \le v \le h$.
   313	  Differentiation at the moving endpoint gives
   314	  \[
   315	    c'(v) = -A(s+h)\overline{A(s+h-v)}
   316	    +\int_s^{s+h-v}A'(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u.
   317	  \]
   318	  Thus, $c(h) = 0$, $|c(v)| \le hM^2$ and $|c'(v)| \le M^2+hMD$. Splitting the
   319	  covariance square into its two conjugate triangles gives
   320	  \[
   321	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}

   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}

   378	\begin{lemma}[Continuous sine factors]\label{L:masked-continuous-wave}

   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]

   397	  \]

   399	  absolute value at most two times a normalized integral of
   400	  $t^jP_{r'}(t)Q_{\rho'}(t)$, where $j \in \{0,1,2\}$ and $|r'-r|,|\rho'-\rho|
   401	  \le 1$. The integral is over zero, one or two copies of $[0,1]$; with no
   402	  averages, use a one-point probability space. Its parameter dependence is
   403	  continuous in $L^2(0,T)$ by dominated convergence.
   404	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} makes it continuous in $H_a$ as well.
   405	  Thus, the averages are Bochner integrals, and their $H_a$ images agree with
   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
   408	
   409	  Apply Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products} to each integrand with $A(t) = t^j$.
   410	  For $j = 0,1,2$, respectively, $M+hD$ is at most $1$, $T+1$ and $T^2+2T$. In
   411	  every case $(M+hD)^2 \le (1+T)^4$. For real $x,e$, the triangle inequality and
   412	  its reverse imply
   413	  \[
   414	    \frac{\langle x\rangle}{1+|e|}
   415	    \le \langle x+e\rangle \le (1+|e|)\langle x\rangle.

   418	  Because $a-1 < 0$, each altered bracket to the power $a-1$ is at most
   419	  $3^{1-a}$ times the original one. Apply these comparisons, Hilbert Jensen and
   420	  the squared scalar coefficient bound four to obtain
   421	  \eqref{E:masked-continuous-wave}. This proves
   422	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}.

   418	/-- The autocorrelation `c(v) = ∫ Φ(u+v) conj Φ(u) du` over `ℝ`.  For
   419	`Φ = 1_I A` with `I = [s, s+h]` and `0 ≤ v ≤ h` it is the TeX's
   420	`c(v) = ∫_s^{s+h-v} A(u+v) conj A(u) du` (TeX line 312). -/

   427	/-- Auxiliary: a bound `‖Φ‖ ≤ M` forces `M ≥ 0`. -/
   428	theorem M_nonneg_of_bound (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) : 0 ≤ M := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hΦb 0)

   430	/-- Auxiliary: for `Φ` measurable, bounded by `M` and vanishing outside
   431	`[s, s+h]`, the integrand of `acorr Φ v` is integrable. -/
   432	theorem acorr_integrable (hΦm : Measurable Φ) (hΦ0 : ∀ u ∉ Icc s (s + h), Φ u = 0)
   433	    (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) (v : ℝ) : Integrable (fun u => Φ (u + v) * conj (Φ u)) := by
   434	  have hM := M_nonneg_of_bound hΦb
   435	  refine Integrable.mono' (g := (Icc s (s + h)).indicator (fun _ => M * M)) ?_ ?_ ?_
   436	  · exact (continuous_const.integrableOn_Icc).integrable_indicator measurableSet_Icc
   437	  · exact ((hΦm.comp (measurable_add_const v)).mul
   438	      (Complex.continuous_conj.measurable.comp hΦm)).aestronglyMeasurable
   439	  · refine ae_of_all _ fun u => ?_
   440	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   441	    · rw [indicator_of_mem hu, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]
   442	      exact mul_le_mul (hΦb _) (hΦb _) (norm_nonneg _) hM
   443	    · rw [indicator_of_notMem hu, hΦ0 u hu, map_zero, mul_zero, norm_zero]

   445	/-- Auxiliary: pointwise bound of the integrand of `acorr Φ v` by
   446	`M² 1_{[s, s+h-v]}`. -/

   448	    (v u : ℝ) :
   449	    ‖Φ (u + v) * conj (Φ u)‖ ≤ (Icc s (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M) u := by
   450	  have hM := M_nonneg_of_bound hΦb
   451	  by_cases hu : u ∈ Icc s (s + h - v)
   452	  · rw [indicator_of_mem hu, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]
   453	    exact mul_le_mul (hΦb _) (hΦb _) (norm_nonneg _) hM
   454	  · rw [indicator_of_notMem hu]
   455	    have : Φ (u + v) = 0 ∨ Φ u = 0 := by
   456	      by_contra hc
   457	      obtain ⟨hc1, hc2⟩ := not_or.mp hc
   458	      have h1 : u + v ∈ Icc s (s + h) := by
   459	        by_contra h'
   460	        exact hc1 (hΦ0 _ h')
   461	      have h2 : u ∈ Icc s (s + h) := by
   462	        by_contra h'
   463	        exact hc2 (hΦ0 _ h')
   464	      exact hu ⟨h2.1, by linarith [h1.2]⟩
   465	    rcases this with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h0]

   470	    (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) (v : ℝ) :
   471	    ‖acorr Φ v‖ ≤ M * M * max (h - v) 0 := by

   473	  have hi : Integrable ((Icc s (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M)) :=

   475	  refine (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le hi (ae_of_all _ (acorr_integrand_le hΦ0 hΦb v))).trans ?_
   476	  rw [integral_indicator_const _ measurableSet_Icc, Real.volume_real_Icc, smul_eq_mul]

   478	  rw [this, mul_comm]

481	`0 ≤ v ≤ w` (TeX line 318 states `|c'(v)| ≤ M² + hMD`; here no derivative of `c`

   483	theorem acorr_lip (hΦm : Measurable Φ) (hΦ0 : ∀ u ∉ Icc s (s + h), Φ u = 0)
   484	    (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M)
   485	    (hΦl : ∀ x ∈ Icc s (s + h), ∀ y ∈ Icc s (s + h), ‖Φ x - Φ y‖ ≤ D * |x - y|)
   486	    (hh : 0 ≤ h) (hD : 0 ≤ D) {v w : ℝ} (hv : 0 ≤ v) (hvw : v ≤ w) :
   487	    ‖acorr Φ v - acorr Φ w‖ ≤ (M * M + h * M * D) * (w - v) := by

   489	  unfold acorr
   490	  rw [← integral_sub (acorr_integrable hΦm hΦ0 hΦb v) (acorr_integrable hΦm hΦ0 hΦb w)]
   491	  have hi1 : Integrable ((Icc s (s + h)).indicator (fun _ => M * D * (w - v))) :=
   492	    (continuous_const.integrableOn_Icc).integrable_indicator measurableSet_Icc
   493	  have hi2 : Integrable ((Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M)) :=
   494	    (integrableOn_const (by simp)).integrable_indicator measurableSet_Ioc
   495	  have hpt : ∀ u, ‖Φ (u + v) * conj (Φ u) - Φ (u + w) * conj (Φ u)‖ ≤
   496	      (Icc s (s + h)).indicator (fun _ => M * D * (w - v)) u +
   497	        (Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M) u := by
   498	    intro u
   499	    have n1 : 0 ≤ (Icc s (s + h)).indicator (fun _ => M * D * (w - v)) u :=
   500	      indicator_nonneg (fun _ _ => mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hM hD) (by linarith)) u
   501	    have n2 : 0 ≤ (Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M) u :=
   502	      indicator_nonneg (fun _ _ => mul_nonneg hM hM) u
   503	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   504	    · by_cases hw : u + w ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   505	      · have hvI : u + v ∈ Icc s (s + h) := ⟨by linarith [hu.1], by linarith [hw.2]⟩
   506	        rw [← sub_mul, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj, indicator_of_mem hu]
   507	        have hl := hΦl _ hvI _ hw
   508	        have e : |u + v - (u + w)| = w - v := by
   509	          rw [show u + v - (u + w) = -(w - v) by ring, abs_neg, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
   510	        rw [e] at hl
   511	        have : ‖Φ (u + v) - Φ (u + w)‖ * ‖Φ u‖ ≤ D * (w - v) * M :=
   512	          mul_le_mul hl (hΦb u) (norm_nonneg _) ((norm_nonneg _).trans hl)
   513	        nlinarith
   514	      · rw [hΦ0 _ hw, zero_mul, sub_zero]
   515	        by_cases hv' : u + v ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   516	        · have hmem : u ∈ Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v) := by
   517	            refine ⟨?_, by linarith [hv'.2]⟩
   518	            by_contra hc
   519	            exact hw ⟨by linarith [hu.1], by linarith⟩
   520	          rw [indicator_of_mem hmem, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]
   521	          have := mul_le_mul (hΦb (u + v)) (hΦb u) (norm_nonneg _) hM
   522	          linarith
   523	        · rw [hΦ0 _ hv', zero_mul, norm_zero]
   524	          linarith
   525	    · rw [hΦ0 u hu, map_zero, mul_zero, mul_zero, sub_zero, norm_zero]
   526	      linarith
   527	  refine (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le (hi1.add hi2) (ae_of_all _ hpt)).trans ?_
   528	  rw [integral_add' hi1 hi2, integral_indicator_const _ measurableSet_Icc,
   529	    integral_indicator_const _ measurableSet_Ioc, Real.volume_real_Icc, Real.volume_real_Ioc,
   530	    smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]
   531	  rw [show s + h - s = h by ring, show s + h - v - (s + h - w) = w - v by ring,
   532	    max_eq_left hh, max_eq_left (by linarith)]
   533	  apply le_of_eq
   534	  ring

   542	  simp only [add_neg_cancel_right, map_mul, Complex.conj_conj]

   545	/-- Auxiliary: `|c(v)| ≤ M² (h - |v|)_+` for every real `v`. -/
   546	theorem acorr_bound_abs (hΦ0 : ∀ u ∉ Icc s (s + h), Φ u = 0)
   547	    (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) (v : ℝ) :

   560	      (Complex.continuous_conj.measurable.comp (hΦm.comp measurable_snd))).stronglyMeasurable

   581	/-- Auxiliary: the kernel `|v|^{-a}` is integrable on `[-h, h]` for `a < 1`. -/

  1381	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-masked-trig-products-paper
  1382	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.masked_trig_products_paper
  1383	  kind: theorem
  1384	  summary: "With the lemma's hypotheses (0<a<1, T>0, 0<h<=1, [s,s+h] in [0,T], A C^1 on it, M, D as sups, r,rho>=0) and supplied inputs (modes in V, linear emb, modulation bound for all omega): 1_I A P_r Q_rho is in V and ||emb(it)||^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)."
  1385	  keywords: [hilbert-norm, trigonometric-product]
  1386	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1387	  status: reusable
  1388	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-trig-product-bound
  1389	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.trig_product_bound
  1390	  kind: theorem
  1391	  summary: "For a complex seminormed E, V a submodule of R->C, emb : V ->l[C] E, any set I, A, reals C,a,h,M,D: if every mode 1_I A e^(i w t) is in V with ||emb||^2 <= C h^(2-a)(M+hD)^2 <hw>^(a-1), then for a witness hp (derivable) ||emb(1_I A P_r Q_rho)||^2 <= C h^(2-a)(M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)."
  1392	  keywords: [hilbert-norm, trigonometric-product]
  1393	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1394	  status: reusable
  1395	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-trig-product-bound-half
  1396	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.trig_product_bound_half
  1397	  kind: theorem
  1398	  summary: "Same hypotheses as trig_product_bound, incl. the redundant witness hp (no sign conditions on C,a,h,M,D,r,rho): ||emb(1_I A P_r Q_rho)||^2 <= C h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho) / 2, the half bound the proof yields."
  1399	  keywords: [hilbert-norm, trigonometric-product]
  1400	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1401	  status: reusable
  1402	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-prod-fn-mem
  1403	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.prodFn_mem
  1404	  kind: theorem
  1405	  summary: "For a submodule V of R->C, a set I and A : R->C, if 1_I A e^(i w t) is in V for every real w, then 1_I A P_r Q_rho is in V for all P, Q in {cos, sin} and real r, rho."
  1406	  keywords: [submodule, trigonometric-product]
  1407	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1408	  status: reusable
  1409	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-norm-sq-sum-le
  1410	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.norm_sq_sum_le
  1411	  kind: theorem
  1412	  summary: "In a complex seminormed space, for a finset s, c : i -> C and v : i -> E: ||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) * sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2."
  1413	  keywords: [norm-inequality, cauchy-schwarz]
  1414	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1415	  status: reusable
  1416	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-norm-sq-sum-le-inner
  1417	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.norm_sq_sum_le_inner
  1418	  kind: theorem
  1419	  summary: "In a complex inner product space, for a finset s, c : i -> C and v : i -> E: ||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) * sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2."
  1420	  keywords: [norm-inequality, inner-product]
  1421	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1422	  status: reusable
  1423	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-four-mode
  1424	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.four_mode
  1425	  kind: theorem
  1426	  summary: "For P, Q in {cos, sin} and reals r, rho, t: P(rt) Q(rho t) = sum over (sigma,tau) in {+-1}^2 of coef P Q (sigma,tau) * exp(i (sigma r + tau rho) t)."
  1427	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1428	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1429	  status: reusable
  1430	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-cos-cos-expand
  1431	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.cos_cos_expand
  1432	  kind: theorem
  1433	  summary: "For reals r, rho, t, in C: cos(rt) cos(rho t) = (1/4)(e^(i(r+rho)t) + e^(i(r-rho)t) + e^(i(-r+rho)t) + e^(i(-r-rho)t))."
  1434	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1435	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1436	  status: reusable
  1437	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-sin-sin-expand
  1438	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.sin_sin_expand
  1439	  kind: theorem
  1440	  summary: "For reals r, rho, t, in C: sin(rt) sin(rho t) = -(1/4)e^(i(r+rho)t) + (1/4)e^(i(r-rho)t) + (1/4)e^(i(-r+rho)t) - (1/4)e^(i(-r-rho)t)."
  1441	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1442	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1443	  status: reusable
  1444	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-sin-cos-expand
  1445	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.sin_cos_expand
  1446	  kind: theorem
  1447	  summary: "For reals r, rho, t, in C: sin(rt) cos(rho t) = -(i/4)e^(i(r+rho)t) - (i/4)e^(i(r-rho)t) + (i/4)e^(i(-r+rho)t) + (i/4)e^(i(-r-rho)t)."
  1448	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1449	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1450	  status: reusable
  1451	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-cos-sin-expand
  1452	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.cos_sin_expand
  1453	  kind: theorem
  1454	  summary: "For reals r, rho, t, in C: cos(rt) sin(rho t) = -(i/4)e^(i(r+rho)t) + (i/4)e^(i(r-rho)t) - (i/4)e^(i(-r+rho)t) + (i/4)e^(i(-r-rho)t)."
  1455	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1456	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1457	  status: reusable
  1458	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-norm-coef
  1459	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.norm_coef
  1460	  kind: theorem
  1461	  summary: "For P, Q in {cos, sin} and every sign pair j, the mode coefficient satisfies |coef P Q j| = 1/4."
  1462	  keywords: [exponential-modes, coefficient-bound]
  1463	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1464	  status: reusable
  1465	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-sum-norm-coef
  1466	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.sum_norm_coef
  1467	  kind: theorem
  1468	  summary: "For P, Q in {cos, sin}, the sum over the four sign pairs j of |coef P Q j| equals 1."
  1469	  keywords: [exponential-modes, coefficient-bound]
  1470	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1471	  status: reusable
  1472	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-prod-fn-eq
  1473	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.prodFn_eq
  1474	  kind: theorem
  1475	  summary: "For any set I, A : R->C, P, Q in {cos, sin} and reals r, rho: the function 1_I A P_r Q_rho equals sum over j of coef P Q j times the mode 1_I A e^(i freq_j t), freq_j = sigma r + tau rho."
  1476	  keywords: [exponential-modes, trigonometric-product]
  1477	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1478	  status: reusable
  1479	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-sum-bracket-freq
  1480	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.sum_bracket_freq
  1481	  kind: theorem
  1482	  summary: "For reals a, h, r, rho: the sum over the four sign pairs j of <h freq_j>^(a-1) equals 2 Q_h(r,rho) = 2(<h(r-rho)>^(a-1) + <h(r+rho)>^(a-1))."
  1483	  keywords: [japanese-bracket, frequency-pair]
  1484	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1485	  status: reusable
  1486	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-trig-eval-expand
  1487	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.Trig.eval_expand
  1488	  kind: theorem
  1489	  summary: "For k in {cos, sin} and real x: k(x) = coef1 k (+) e^(ix) + coef1 k (-) e^(-ix), i.e. cos x = (e^(ix)+e^(-ix))/2 and sin x = (-i/2)e^(ix) + (i/2)e^(-ix)."
  1490	  keywords: [trigonometric-identity, exponential-modes]
  1491	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1492	  status: internal
  1493	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-trig-products-exp-sgn
  1494	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedTrigProducts.exp_sgn
  1495	  kind: theorem
  1496	  summary: "For a sign sigma and real x: exp(i sgn(sigma) x) is exp(i x) when sigma is + and exp(-(i x)) when sigma is -."
  1497	  keywords: [exponential-modes, sign]
  1498	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean
  1499	  status: internal

  1502	  kind: theorem
  1503	  summary: "For k in {cos, sin} and a sign sigma, |coef1 k sigma| = 1/2."
  1504	  keywords: [exponential-modes, coefficient-bound]
  1505	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedTrigProducts.lean

4335	# --- MaskedModulation (StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean) ---
  4336	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-masked-temporal-modulation-paper
  4337	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.masked_temporal_modulation_paper
  4338	  kind: theorem
  4339	  summary: "With 0<a<1, T>0, 0<h<=1, 0<=s, s+h<=T, A C^1 on I=[s,s+h], M=sup_I|A|, D=sup_I|A'|, real omega: F=1_I A e^(i omega t) gives an integrable integrand on [0,T]^2 and |timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)."
  4340	  keywords: [temporal-modulation, oscillatory-bound]
  4341	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4342	  status: reusable
  4343	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-modulation-bound
  4344	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.modulation_bound
  4345	  kind: theorem
  4346	  summary: "If 0<a<1, h>0, 0<=s, s+h<=T, A continuous on I=[s,s+h], |A|<=M on I and |A x - A y| <= D|x-y| on I: for every real omega, F=1_I A e^(i omega t) has integrable integrand on [0,T]^2 and |timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)."
  4347	  keywords: [temporal-modulation, oscillatory-bound]
  4348	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4349	  status: reusable
  4350	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-masked-trig-products-bridged-paper
  4351	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper
  4352	  kind: theorem
  4353	  summary: "With the hypotheses of masked_trig_products_paper, but hnorm (|emb f|^2 = Re timeForm a T f f for f in V with f in L^2(0,T)) in place of hmod; hmem (modes in V, emb linear) kept: 1_I A P_r Q_rho is in V and |emb(it)|^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)."
  4354	  keywords: [trigonometric-product, norm-identity]
  4355	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4356	  status: reusable
  4357	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr
  4358	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr
  4359	  kind: definition
  4360	  summary: "acorr Phi v = int_R Phi(u+v) conj(Phi u) du (Bochner; Lean's 0 if not integrable). For Phi = 1_I A and 0 <= v <= h it is the c(v) of the proof of L:masked-temporal-modulation."
  4361	  keywords: [autocorrelation, temporal-modulation]
  4362	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4363	  status: reusable
  4364	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-bound
  4365	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_bound
  4366	  kind: theorem
  4367	  summary: "If Phi = 0 outside [s,s+h] and |Phi u| <= M for all u: for every real v, |acorr Phi v| <= M*M*max(h - v, 0)."
  4368	  keywords: [autocorrelation, envelope-bound]
  4369	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4370	  status: reusable
  4371	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-lip
  4372	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_lip
  4373	  kind: theorem
  4374	  summary: "If Phi measurable, = 0 outside I=[s,s+h], |Phi| <= M, |Phi x - Phi y| <= D|x-y| on I, h >= 0, D >= 0, 0 <= v <= w: |acorr Phi v - acorr Phi w| <= (M*M + h*M*D)(w - v)."
  4375	  keywords: [autocorrelation, lipschitz-bound]
  4376	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4377	  status: reusable
  4378	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-neg
  4379	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_neg
  4380	  kind: theorem
  4381	  summary: "For every Phi : R -> C and real v: acorr Phi (-v) = conj(acorr Phi v)."
  4382	  keywords: [autocorrelation, conjugate-symmetry]
  4383	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean

   362	
   363	Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
   364	interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
   365	unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
   366	the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
   367	`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
   368	`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
   369	`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
   370	`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
   371	kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
   372	(`L:masked-continuous-wave`; defined in Lean as `MaskedContinuousWave.bFn`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
   373	change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
   374	`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
   375	zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
   376	are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
   377	`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in

  2186	## MaskedTrigProducts (whole result)
  2187	
  2188	Formalizes `L:masked-trig-products` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
  2189	at `ba01d98`): for `P_r` in `{cos(rt), sin(rt)}` and `Q_rho` in
  2190	`{cos(rho t), sin(rho t)}`, the bound `E:masked-trig-products`,
  2191	`||1_I A P_r Q_rho||_a^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)`, with
  2192	`Q_h` as in `E:masked-frequency-pair` and `<x> = sqrt(1+x^2)`. All four
  2193	`cos`/`sin` combinations are covered, together with every step of the
  2194	proof: the four-mode expansion (coefficients of absolute value `1/4`,
  2195	frequencies `+-r +- rho`), the Hilbert-space inequality
  2196	`||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2`, and the frequency
  2197	count (two modes at `|r-rho|`, two at `r+rho`).
  2198	The norm `||.||_a` is modelled abstractly. The manuscript's norm is that of
  2199	the complexified temporal completion `H_a^C` of `L:masked-time-completion`,
  2200	and functions enter it through the linear inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. In Lean,
  2201	`E` stands for that completion (for the concrete completion see
  2202	`TimeCompletion`; a complex inner product space in the
  2203	paper wrapper, a complex seminormed space in the general theorems).
  2204	`V : Submodule C (R -> C)` is the class of functions accepted into it, and
  2205	`emb : V ->l[C] E` is the inclusion, so `||emb f||` stands for `||f||_a`.
  2206	This is faithful because the proof uses only linearity of the inclusion: it
  2207	writes the product as a linear combination of four modes and bounds each
  2208	mode. Two inputs are supplied as named hypotheses. `hmem` says that every
  2209	mode `1_I A e^(i omega t)` lies in `V` (from `L:masked-time-completion`).
  2210	`hmod` is the bound `E:masked-temporal-modulation` of
  2211	`L:masked-temporal-modulation` for every real `omega`, stated in the
  2212	manuscript's form with `C0(a) = 16/(1-a)`. These two inputs stay as they
  2213	are for `masked_trig_products_paper` and the general theorems below.
  2214	`MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` (see "MaskedModulation
  2215	(whole result)") keeps `hmem` and replaces `hmod` by the norm identity
  2216	`hnorm`, `||emb f||^2` = the real part of the defining double integral of
  2217	`f(t) conj f(s) |t-s|^(-a)`, required only for `f` in `V` that lie in
  2218	`L^2(0,T)`; it proves the modulation bound. The product function is never
  2219	assumed to satisfy a bound, and its membership in `V` is not an independent
  2220	assumption of the paper wrapper: `prodFn_mem` derives it from `hmem`. The
  2221	general theorems `trig_product_bound` and `trig_product_bound_half` take a
  2222	membership witness `hp`, which is redundant for the same reason. Implicit hypotheses made explicit in
  2223	`masked_trig_products_paper`: `A` is a function on the reals (only its
  2224	values on `I` matter, because of the indicator); `C^1(I; C)` is
  2225	`ContDiffOn R 1 A I`; `M` and `D` are the `sSup` of `||A||` and of
  2226	`||derivWithin A I||` over `I`; `I = Icc s (s+h)`. The wrapper also carries
  2227	the standing hypotheses `0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `0 < h <= 1`, `0 <= s`,
  2228	`s + h <= T`, `C^1`, the definitions of `M` and `D`, and `r, rho >= 0`.
  2229	These are carried but unused by the proof; they are consumed by the
  2230	supplied modulation input. The general theorems `trig_product_bound` and
  2231	`trig_product_bound_half` hold for arbitrary real `C, a, h, M, D, r, rho`
  2232	and any set `I`. The sign conditions on `r, rho` are unnecessary because
  2233	`<.>` is even. `trig_product_bound_half` is sharper than the stated lemma: it
  2234	records the factor `1/2` that the proof yields ("one half of the asserted
  2235	right side"). `L:masked-temporal-modulation` and the bound
  2236	`E:masked-time-schur` are now formalized for the defining double integral
  2237	(`MaskedModulation`, `TimeSchur`). The completion `H_a` of
  2238	`L:masked-time-completion`, the identification of its norm with the double
  2239	integral and the extension from `L^2(0,T)` are formalized in
  2240	`TimeCompletion`. They enter this module's wrappers through `hmem` and
  2241	`hmod` (and through `hmem` and `hnorm` in the bridged wrapper), and
  2242	`TimeCompletion.masked_trig_products_completed_paper` discharges both, so
  2243	`L:masked-trig-products` holds with nothing supplied.

    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,

    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.

    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}

    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put

    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and

    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
